title: Beyond the Numbers | The Long Math
description: Beyond the Numbers applies The Long Math's arithmetic-first lens to careers, training pipelines, medicine, professional life, and other long-horizon decisions where opportunity cost, delayed earnings, taxation, and cash-flow timing matter.
heroLede: Long-horizon arithmetic for careers, training, and the structure of a life.
introP1: Some of the most important financial decisions in life are not investment decisions. They are decisions about careers, training, geography, family structure, and how a life is built over decades.
introP2: Beyond the Numbers expands the lens of The Long Math to long-horizon decisions where delayed earnings, opportunity cost, debt, taxation, incentives, and cash-flow timing become central to the outcome. These essays apply the same arithmetic-first thinking used throughout the site to questions that extend beyond investing alone.
introP3: Many of the early essays focus on medicine because it is the professional world I know personally and because few careers involve longer training pipelines, more delayed compounding, or more financially unusual timelines. Over time, this section will expand into other professions, career structures, and major life decisions where the long-term math meaningfully shapes the outcome.

featured.title: Is Medical School Financially Worth It?
featured.excerpt: Medicine is one of the most respected professions in society. It is also one of the longest and most financially unusual career paths. This essay examines the full financial timeline of becoming a physician — from tuition and residency income to the delayed compounding that follows.
